complexity.correctness_reason: Float division in the arrival-time comparison loses precision once the caps on target/position/speed are lifted: with sufficiently large integers, two distinct rational arrival times can differ by less than a double's ulp (e.g. consecutive Farey-style ratios d1/s1 vs d2/s2 with d,s ~ 2^40) and compare equal or inverted, merging or splitting fleets wrongly.
complexity.notes: Sorting ascending and popping from the end processes cars nearest the target first, which is correct. Unused `import math`. Using exact integer cross-multiplication ((target-p1)*s2 vs (target-p2)*s1) instead of float division would make comparisons exact for arbitrarily large values.
complexity.summary: Sorts cars by position, then scans from closest-to-target backwards, comparing each car's arrival time (target-pos)/speed against the current lead fleet's arrival time via float division; a strictly later lead time starts a new fleet.
